subject: Orion Health — post-call recap & tactical bakeoff plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@orionhealth.com>, Tim Reynolds <tim.reynolds@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Orion Health — post-call recap & tactical bakeoff plan

Hi Sophie + Tim — thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

TL;DR: Orion wants a short head-to-head POC vs Hyperscaler A to validate latency, cost, and hallucination profile on 6 clinical prompt templates. We proposed a 2-week bakeoff; below is the tactical plan, owners, and success criteria.

What we heard from you
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost and P90 latency compared to your current Hyperscaler A endpoints while preserving clinical accuracy (extracted values + instruction-following).
- Constraints: PHI is in-scope for the POC (will provide redacted samples), preferred region: us-east, want private VPC option if possible.
- Success signals: end-to-end latency, per-prompt QA pass rate (clinician-reviewed), and token-unit cost delta.

Proposed bakeoff (2-week sprint) — high level
1) Baseline collection (3 days): we run 500 requests across your 6 prompt templates against your current Hyperscaler A endpoints.
2) Redwood run (4 days): run same workload on Redwood Hosted + Dedicated config variants.
3) Metrics + eval (3 days): compute latency percentiles, cost-per-1M-tokens estimate, and qualitative QA checks using clinician-labeled gold set.
4) Wrap & Next steps (2 days): executive summary + recommendation.

Owners (tentative)
- Redwood PM / POC lead: Tessa Morgan — overall coordinator + client comms
- Sales / Commercial: Vivek Kulkarni — pricing/contracting and Dedicated sizing
- Solutions / Eval design: Marissa Cole — eval set, scoring, clinician QA plan
- Benchmarks / infra: Ben Carter, Rishi Malhotra — test harness, run scripts, telemetry capture

Success criteria (for go/no-go recommendation)
- Latency: Redwood P90 <= Hyperscaler A P90 * 0.9 (i.e., at least 10% P90 improvement) OR absolute P90 < 200ms for typical 1k-token sessions.
- Cost: projected token-unit cost for Redwood <= Hyperscaler A after applying batching/kv-cache assumptions.
- Quality: clinician QA pass-rate delta <= 2% drop vs Hyperscaler A on extraction templates; any regression must be explained by prompt adjustments or model variant.
- Operational: ability to run in us-east and provide VPC/private deployment option for final phase.

Attachments I’m sharing (v1): bakeoff_test_plan_v1.xlsx (test matrix + timeline), sample_eval_prompts.jsonl (anonymized examples), mop_draft.md (minimal ops playbook). Drive + HubSpot links at bottom.

Immediate asks for Orion
- Confirm PHI handling approach and whether you can share a scrubbed sample set by EOD Wed, Dec 22.
- Confirm stakeholders for clinician QA (names + availability).
- Confirm commitment to a two-week slot starting Mon, Dec 27 (suggested kickoff Dec 27).

If this looks good I’ll loop in Ben/Rishi offline to lock test harness and Vivek to confirm pricing guardrails. Happy to jump on a 20m sync tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: bakeoff_test_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_eval_prompts.jsonl (data), mop_draft.md (markdown))

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@orionhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:04:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Orion Health — post-call recap & tactical bakeoff plan

Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear plan. Confirming a few items from our side:

- PHI samples: we can provide 100 de-identified examples by EOD Wed (we will remove MRNs and patient names but keep clinical phrasing).
- Clinician reviewers: Dr. Maya Patel and Nurse Lead Carlos Vega will be available for spot checks (we’ll share availability tomorrow).
- Timing: Dec 27 kickoff works but note we have limited engineering coverage Dec 28–29 (holiday overlap). If Redwood can front-load the baseline collection and mock runs before those dates, that would help.

Two asks:
1) Can you include a short SOC2/Security brief for the POC (we need to submit to our procurement team)?
2) We’d like to include a Hyperscaler A + Hyperscaler B baseline if possible; Hyperscaler B is cheaper but we think performance may vary. Can Redwood run both if we provide credentials?

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Integrations, Orion Health
